text:
incident-bot: PAGE: GeoDNS answers inconsistent across CF/Route53 + resolver spikes affecting api.redwood.ai. Severity: P2. Paging oncall.

maya: seeing elevated 5xxs from EU customers, started ~08:12 UTC. Traces show DNS lookups returning mixed A answers across regions.

ev an: can you paste a dig from one of the affected regions? suspect cached stale TTLs + external resolver flapping.

maya: sure. from probe in eu-west-1:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
54.72.10.21
54.72.10.21
```
from probe in us-east-1:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
3.120.99.12
54.72.10.21
```
```
so some resolvers return old IPs that route to an AZ with partial network degradation.
```

alex: confirmed. Cloudfront health checks show origin in eu-west-2 had intermittent egress issues around same time. Route53 geo routing + Cloudflare load balancing are both in play for this name.

oncall-amber: I'm on. paging in netops and cs.

netops: joining. what's the customer impact? are users seeing 502/504 or connection timeouts?

maya: majority are 502/504 from our edge -> in-region origin failovers. Some mobile clients get connection refused when they hit the stale IP that points to a decommissioned AZ host.

sam-cs: flagged to a couple of enterprise customers, they reported spike in failures starting 08:10.

evan: quick mitigation plan:
1) reduce DNS TTL to 30s for api.redwood.ai (both CF LB + Route53) to accelerate convergence
2) temporarily remove the stale origin IP from the geo-sets in Route53
3) enable CF origin fallback to secondary pool
4) monitor success rate and sweep resolver caches by nudging authoritative answers

maya: I can apply the TTL change on CF LB now. Alex can you coordinate Route53 edit?

alex: on it. changing Route53 record set TTL from 300 -> 30 and removing the stale IP entry from the eu geo-policy. Applying now.

incident-bot: DEPLOYMENT: dns-change-3151234567 TTL update started by alex.

alex: Route53 change pushed. note: propagation may take ~30-120s depending on resolver. I also removed the stale IP from the geo policy.

maya: CF LB config updated TTL -> 30 and failover enabled.

netops: running active probes across resolvers. initial dig sweep:
```
1.1.1.1 -> 54.72.10.21
8.8.8.8 -> 3.120.99.12
9.9.9.9 -> 54.72.10.21
2001:4860:4860::8888 -> 3.120.99.12
```
some resolvers still returning the stale IPs. likely cached upstream. we'll watch for convergence.

evan: while that converges we should also add a temporary proxy-level redirect: if request from edge hits backend with IP A and origin health failing, route to healthy pool to avoid 502s. Maya, can you enable proxy fallback rule?

maya: enabling fallback rule. rule id: pf-2026-temporary-fallback. Pushing now.

incident-bot: CHANGE: proxy rule pf-2026-temporary-fallback enabled by maya.

alex: CF reports fewer origin errors after enabling fallback. error rate down from 6% -> 1.2% in last 3m.

sam-cs: passed note to customers: "We're seeing DNS propagation issues affecting a subset of requests; we've shortened TTLs and enabled failover. We will follow up with RCA." They appreciate the quick update.

netops: still seeing a small set of resolvers returning stale answers from an ISP-level cache in APAC. Short-term we can add an alias pointing to healthy IPs for that geo policy, but prefer letting TTL expire.

evan: agree. avoid complex routing churn. continue to monitor for 30m. If errors don't drop to <0.5% we'll start contacting Cloudflare support to look at edge-level cache.

maya: metrics now: 1m error rate 0.9%, p99 latency back to baseline in most regions. EU still slightly elevated.

alex: opening ticket with Cloudflare and Route53 support with dig traces and timestamps. Ticket IDs:
- CF: 9876543
- AWS: 7654321

incident-bot: TICKET_CREATED: CF#9876543 AWS#7654321 by alex.

netops: starting to annotate affected customers list for post-incident comms. Any evidence of data loss? auth logs look normal.

maya: no data loss. just request-level failures. All critical paths preserved via fallback.

oncall-amber: handing off to evan for monitoring window. I'm going offline now but reachable if things spike. Evan, you own the incident until 09:30 UTC.

evan: taking handoff. monitoring dashboard pinned. will escalate to SRE lead if error rate >1.5% for 5m.

sam-cs: will prepare a more detailed customer-facing blurb once we have Cloudflare/AWS updates.

netops: quick note for postmortem: check geoDNS sync windows, TTL hygiene between CF and Route53, and our runbook step ordering (TTL change before record removal?).

evan: agreed. adding runbook TODO to incident ticket.

maya: thanks team. keeping this thread updated with probe sweeps and sigs.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: status=monitoring, severity=P2, owner=evan, started=3151234567. Next update scheduled 08:45 UTC.

maya: probe sweep @08:28
```
8.8.8.8 -> 3.120.99.12
1.1.1.1 -> 3.120.99.12
9.9.9.9 -> 3.120.99.12
```
looks like convergence is mostly done.

evan: error rate holding ~0.4% last 5m. leaving TTL at 30 for 1h before restoring to 300. will close incident if stable for 30m.

sam-cs: sending customers updated note: "We've applied mitigations; service stabilized. We're investigating root cause and will follow up with RCA." :thumbsup:

netops: adding final checklist for RCA: correlate CF edge cache invalidation times, Route53 change events, and origin egress queue spikes.

oncall-amber: thanks all, nice rapid coordination. handing archive to evan.

incident-bot: INCIDENT_RESOLVED: status=resolved_by_monitoring, closed_at=3151235120, summary="GeoDNS/External resolver propagation caused mixed A answers -> TTL reduction + failover reduced impact."
